prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Scope: offshore generation assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external organizations, control, maintenance. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick; electrical collection/switching), export connection to Grid Interface Relay (external grid interface). Out of scope: public grid beyond connection point; non-farm port operations. Architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services and shore decision functions with defined interfaces. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; local turbine control; produces Pitch Deviation Notice for operational handling), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor (distinct), Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (blade assessment). Substation: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor. Cooperating shore/ops parts: SCADA Gateway (alias Juniper Vale; controlled boundary mediating supervisory data exchange between offshore assets and shore), Shore Control Room (alias Amber Quay; principal shore monitoring/coordination, shared operational context, dispatch coordination), Maintenance Planning Engine (alias Thistle Crown; organizes maintenance needs, resources, constraints; supports, not replaces, Duty Planner). Fleet Dispatch Console: fleet-level dispatch view. Marine resources: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck (helicopter access). Personnel Tracking Console (location/accountability), North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System, Spares Hub (inventory/logistics). Enabling: Work Permit Portal (work authorization), Cybersecurity Gateway, communications, fire protection, backup power. Actors: SCADA Engineer (maintains supervisory interface configuration/integrity), Control Engineer (assesses status, coordinates response using shore picture), Duty Planner (uses Maintenance Planning Engine), Marine Coordinator (weighs conditions, vessel availability for access). External: Weather Service (alias Pale Lantern; provides environmental info), Metocean Buoy (observations), grid operations, ports, suppliers, emergency services. Requirements: work shall be authorized, hazards controlled, personnel/vessels accounted for; prevent pollution, minimize marine disturbance, respond promptly to environmental incidents. Modes: commissioning/acceptance (documented handover), normal service (validated status, procedures, forecasts, grid instructions), planned maintenance, unplanned maintenance (prioritized fault assessment, severity-based mobilization), major refurbishment, decommissioning (isolation, removal planning, record transfer).

New part:
S071: The Cybersecurity Gateway provides a security boundary for connected operational services.
S072: The architecture assigns defined responsibilities to interfaces so that system changes can be assessed and managed.
S073: Operational personnel retain authority for decisions that require procedural, safety, or engineering judgment.
S074: This arrangement supports maintainable operations while keeping supervisory functions distinct from planning and human coordination.
S075: The operating organization combines shore-based planning, marine coordination, vessel crews, and technicians assigned to offshore work.
S076: The Duty Planner develops daily work priorities with input from the Field Supervisor and the Maintenance Planning Engine.
S077: The Marine Coordinator aligns vessel availability with crew readiness, port access, and the planned work locations.
S078: The Crew Transfer Vessel is identified in local procedures by the alias Kestrel Bay.
S079: The Vessel Master retains authority for navigation, vessel safety, and decisions about whether a transfer can proceed.
S080: The Fleet Dispatch Console is identified in local procedures by the alias Sable Orchard.
S081: The Fleet Dispatch Console gives the Marine Coordinator a shared view of vessel assignments, planned movements, and dispatch status.
S082: The Marine Coordinator uses that view to coordinate the Crew Transfer Vessel, the Service Operations Vessel, and the Daughter Craft as conditions require.
S083: The Weather Service produces the Squall Window Bulletin for operational awareness.
S084: The Weather Analyst reviews available forecasts and advises the Marine Coordinator on conditions that may affect marine operations.
S085: The Vessel Master evaluates local conditions before departure and continues to reassess them during the voyage.
S086: A Weather Hold pauses affected marine activity until the responsible personnel confirm that operations can resume safely.
S087: The Crew Transfer Vessel transports authorized personnel and routine tools between shore and offshore work locations.
S088: The Daughter Craft can support short-range transfers when the operating plan and conditions permit its use.
S089: The Service Operations Vessel provides a platform for work that needs longer offshore presence or broader onboard support.
S090: The Warehouse System is identified in local procedures by the alias Mosslight.
S091: The Warehouse System records stock status and supports preparation of equipment and consumables for scheduled work.
S092: The Storekeeper checks requested materials against available stock and coordinates replenishment with the Spares Hub.
S093: The Port Agent supports shore-side arrangements for vessel calls, crew access, and staged cargo.
S094: The Personnel Tracking Console helps the organization maintain an accurate view of personnel assigned to offshore activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
